_about: W3C DID Method Rubric (https://www.w3.org/TR/did-rubric/) scoring template used as the qualitative axis (framework §7). Scores: 1 (best) – 4 (worst) per the rubric's own response scales, or 'tbd'. Every non-tbd cell must cite a file:line or a measured value from results/metrics/latest. assessor = who scored; reviewed = independent check done?

criteria.name: Rulemaking
criteria.question: Who can change the DID method rules?

criteria.name: Design and operation
criteria.question: Who designs and operates the method infrastructure?

criteria.name: Open contribution
criteria.question: Can anyone contribute to the specification/implementation?

criteria.name: Key rotation
criteria.question: Can the controller rotate keys without changing the DID?

criteria.name: Deactivation
criteria.question: Can the DID be deactivated and resolve as such?

criteria.name: DID Document integrity
criteria.question: Can a resolver verify the document was not tampered with?

criteria.name: Correlation risk
criteria.question: Does use of the DID create linkable records?

criteria.name: PII in DID Document
criteria.question: Does the method require/encourage PII on the ledger?

criteria.name: Scalability
criteria.question: Cost/latency behaviour as the registry grows (from L3)

criteria.name: Storage footprint
criteria.question: Persistent state per identity (from L1 newSlots / L2 totals)

criteria.name: Decentralised operation
criteria.question: Any single point of operational control?
